jurisdiction.name: Palau
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Palau has no AI law, AI strategy or AI guidance, and no general data protection law. The only related national instrument is the July 2026 Cybersecurity Act, which creates a Bureau of Cybersecurity and sets security duties for personal data held by government agencies but contains no AI provisions. A presidential Office of Applied Technology and Strategy created in April 2026 is known only from news reports.
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026 from the National Congress's website and the national government portal; Palau has no official gazette. Not yet verified from the official text: material from the financial institutions commission and the judiciary. The Cybersecurity Act, a pending digital infrastructure bill and the new technology office are tracked as leads.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Palau's national congress bill tracker, the national government portal and its executive orders, ministries and regulators were searched, and no qualifying AI-governance document was found in any category. Palau has no official gazette, and the financial regulator's and the judiciary's websites remain to be checked. Not yet verified from the official text: a privacy law cited only by unofficial sites and the official text of an April 2026 executive order creating an Office of Applied Technology and Strategy.

leads.title: Executive order establishing the Office of Applied Technology and Strategy within the Office of the President
leads.english_title: Executive order establishing the Office of Applied Technology and Strategy (April 2026)
leads.issuing_authority: Office of the President of the Republic of Palau
leads.note: Reported (news, April 2026) as signed by President Whipps to centralise government technology planning, cybersecurity and e-government; the President's remarks mention AI use as a topic. No official text, number or date found: the executive orders list on palaugov.pw stops at EO No. 478 and the site search returns nothing for it. Record only if the official order is published and sets expectations for AI (otherwise out of scope as a general technology office).

leads.title: National Digital Infrastructure and Cybersecurity Framework Act (Bill 2025/3)
leads.english_title: National Digital Infrastructure and Cybersecurity Framework Act
leads.issuing_authority: Olbiil Era Kelulau (House of Delegates; proposed by Hon. Brian Melairei)
leads.note: Pending bill listed at https://palauoek.org/bills/national-digital-infrastructure-cybersecurity-framework-act/ (introduced 20 August 2025, assigned to Standing Committee on Education, no further progress). Summary on the page: a Palau Digital Authority overseeing broadband, data governance and cybersecurity; mandatory data-protection protocols for government networks; a national data centre. The 'Download PDF' link is a blank page, so the text could not be read; no AI provision confirmed.

leads.title: An Act to create a comprehensive cybersecurity system in the Republic of Palau; and to amend section 604 of Title 7 of the Palau National Code and for other related purposes (RPPL No. 12-8, the "Cybersecurity Act")
leads.english_title: Cybersecurity Act (RPPL No. 12-8): Act creating a comprehensive cybersecurity system in the Republic of Palau
leads.issuing_authority: Olbiil Era Kelulau (Palau National Congress); approved by the President of the Republic of Palau
leads.note: Moved to leads under the PROTOCOL §1 scope test: the Act contains no AI provision (its only technology hook is a duty to 'continuously study emergent technology'); it is a cybersecurity law with security and confidentiality duties for personal data held by agencies, not a general data protection law. Official PDF: https://palauoek.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/RPPL-No.-12-8.pdf (approved 2026-07-21; takes effect on approval, s.3).
